explanation: The main character in the Book of Job, a righteous and wealthy man who undergoes enormous trials and suffering.
An evil spiritual being who challenges Job and his faithfulness to God by inflicting suffering upon him.
The great difficulties and challenges that Job faces throughout the story, including loss of wealth, health, and family.
Job's enduring trust and loyalty to God, even when he confronts seemingly unexplainable suffering.
Three individuals (Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar) who visit Job to comfort and advise him during his trials. They represent different perspectives on why Job suffers.
A younger man who offers his opinion on Job's situation and criticizes both Job and his friends for their lack of understanding of God's wisdom.
The Almighty Creator who ultimately speaks to Job and his friends, revealing insight into His sovereignty and wisdom.
A central theme in the Book of Job concerning seeking and understanding God's will and purposes, even when they do not immediately make sense to human reason.
